candidates.title: Draft booking and status notifications

demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: booking confirmations, provider assignment notifications, payment status updates, and customer alerts

ease.reason: A fictional booking can produce a notification draft, but no supplied reference documents webhook or messaging setup.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: on-demand service operators might pay for notification setup; this post shows no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can draft alerts from sample booking states; API access, retries, and duplicate prevention remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: The proposed event-to-alert loop repeats, but execution is unsupported and a person must verify payment state and failures.

evidence.reason: The retained span explicitly names confirmations, assignments, payment updates, alerts, retries, and duplicate prevention.

experimentPlan.output: A proposed set of booking status message drafts based on operator-supplied sample events.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits a sample booking event for a notification draft.
steps: Draft one customer or provider message.
Have an operator review the draft before sending.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For fixed sample events, verify the selected template and recipient role match a manually prepared expected result.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An operator supplies templates and validates booking and payment status; no message is sent without human authorization.

candidates.reason: Concrete chore assessed as a proposed sample-data experiment; provisional mean is below 6 because no supplied implementation reference supports its mechanics.

candidates.title: Sort sample emails into review folders

demandEvidence.chore: Sort sample emails into review folders

ease.reason: The Code node documentation supports data transformation and logic, and the If node supports conditional branching; neither establishes mailbox integration.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small professional service firms might pay for inbox sorting; this post shows a task, not buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week prototype can apply operator-defined rules to fictional messages; live mailbox access and classification quality remain untested.

autonomy.reason: A proposed classify-and-route loop is repeatable; documented Code and If nodes support logic and branching, while a person reviews uncertain matches.

evidence.reason: The retained spans describe automatic email sorting and text matching and Boolean routing problems; frequency and broader demand are unknown.

experimentPlan.output: A proposed folder label for each sample email plus a review flag when its rule match is unclear.
inputs: Expected folder label for each sample
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits a sample message batch for sorting.
steps: Apply each operator-defined phrase rule to the sample text.
Use a conditional branch for matched versus unmatched messages.
Flag ambiguous or unmatched examples for review.
Compare labels with expected results and revise rules.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a fixed fictional test set, compare every proposed label and review flag with operator-prepared expected results.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person defines rules, checks false matches, and authorizes any live mailbox access or folder changes.

candidates.reason: The literal sorting chore supports a bounded experiment; the n8n Code and If documentation supports transformation and branching only. Honest provisional mean is below 6.
